report.summary: Reviewed chunk 1/2 of graph_brief.py: module docstring, dataclass GraphBrief, file_symbols, _deep_only_modules, _tail_matches, _neighbourhood, graph_brief (partial). Claims about behaviour checked against visible code.
risks: _deep_only_modules | low | Uses ast.walk on parsed tree; if tree has many nodes, could be slow for large files. | Profile on repo's largest files.
_tail_matches | medium | Suffix matching may over-match, mislabeling edges as deep when they are not (though doc says it only adds a * mark). | Review over-match cases in actual usage.
graph_brief | medium | Catches BaseException (not shown in chunk) which may suppress signals like KeyboardInterrupt. | Check full implementation.
graph_brief | low | Cached index is single-flight; if a lane cannot get an index it runs without brief, which could silently degrade quality. | Ensure fallback logging is in place.

handoff.purpose: Define module docstring, constants, dataclass GraphBrief, and helper functions for building a three-layer graph brief.

symbols.name: DEFAULT_BUDGET_CHARS
symbols.note: Default character budget for a whole brief, set to 12000.

symbols.name: DEEP_EDGE_MARK
symbols.note: Marks an edge that exists only inside a function body, value '*'.

symbols.name: ARTEFACT_ROOTS
symbols.note: Tuple of path prefixes that are artefacts and must never appear in a brief: ('runs/', 'build/', 'dist/', '.captures/').

symbols.name: _HEADER_RESERVE
symbols.note: Characters reserved for the header, set to 700.

symbols.name: _is_artefact
symbols.note: Returns True if rel starts with any of ARTEFACT_ROOTS.

symbols.name: GraphBrief
symbols.note: Dataclass representing a rendered brief plus the facts it was rendered from.

symbols.name: GraphBrief.text
symbols.note: str: The rendered text of the brief.

symbols.name: GraphBrief.targets
symbols.note: tuple[str,...]: Files the brief was requested for.

symbols.name: GraphBrief.neighbours
symbols.note: tuple[str,...]: Files pulled in as graph neighbours.

symbols.name: GraphBrief.counts
symbols.note: Mapping[str,int]: Layer name -> number of items rendered.

symbols.name: GraphBrief.dropped
symbols.note: Mapping[str,int]: Layer name -> number of items dropped by budget.

symbols.name: GraphBrief.provenance
symbols.note: Mapping[str,Any]: Any provenance data, default empty dict.

symbols.name: GraphBrief.char_count
symbols.note: Returns len(self.text).

symbols.name: GraphBrief.truncated
symbols.note: Returns True if any dropped values are truthy.

symbols.name: _sig
symbols.note: Returns a signature string for an ast.FunctionDef or ast.AsyncFunctionDef node.

symbols.name: file_symbols
symbols.note: Returns top-level API of one Python file as declaration lines (signatures).

symbols.name: _deep_only_modules
symbols.note: Returns dotted module names that a file imports only inside a function body.

symbols.name: _tail_matches
symbols.note: Checks if any dotted name in the set plausibly denotes a given relative path via suffix matching.

symbols.name: _neighbourhood
symbols.note: Returns sorted list of neighbours of targets within given hops, excluding artefacts.

symbols.name: graph_brief
symbols.note: Builds the brief for targets and their hops-hop neighbourhood (partial implementation in this chunk).

claims.text: Three layers, which is why it is a brief and not a manifest: 1. symbols -- what exists, per file. Answers 'does this name exist'. 2. imports -- who reaches whom, INCLUDING the edges that live inside function bodies. Answers 'what will I break' and 'where does this belong'. Function-body edges are marked *: 202 of 526 internal edges in this repo are only visible there, so a brief built from top-level imports alone would present ~60% of the graph as the whole of it. 3. documents -- which page claims to describe this file. Answers 'what has someone already promised about this code', which is the layer that turns a docstring lie into a visible contradiction rather than a discovery.
claims.why: Layer 2's claim about 202 of 526 edges is not verifiable from this chunk. Layer 3 (documents) is not implemented in this chunk.

claims.text: Layers 2 and 3 degrade cleanly: the type and document layers of the index are behind flags, and when they are off those sections are omitted rather than faked.
claims.why: No flag handling or index layer logic is visible in this chunk.

claims.text: What is never omitted silently is a TRUNCATION -- if the budget cuts the brief, the brief says what it dropped. A brief that quietly stops listing files reads exactly like a brief that says those files do not exist, which is the hallucination this module was written to prevent.
claims.why: The GraphBrief dataclass has a 'dropped' field and a 'truncated' property, and the docstring describes the design intent. The code in this chunk does not yet show the truncation logic, but the claim about the design is supported by the dataclass fields.

claims.text: This is a DERIVED artefact. It is regenerated, never edited, and a model must not cite it as evidence about behaviour -- it describes shape, not semantics.
claims.why: No evidence in this chunk about how the brief is used or cited.

claims.text: Default character budget for a whole brief. Sized from measurement, not taste: the full symbol layer for the daedalus/ package is 6,479 characters, so a 1-hop brief around a handful of files fits comfortably and the budget only bites on a genuinely wide change.
claims.why: The measurement of the symbol layer size is not verifiable from this chunk.

claims.text: Marks an edge that exists ONLY inside a function body. See the module docstring: this is the 38% of the import graph that naive tooling misses.
claims.why: The 38% claim is not verifiable from this chunk.

claims.text: Path prefixes that are ARTEFACTS, not the project, and must never appear in a brief. Both entries are measured, not defensive: * runs/ -- the first brief built for daedalus/shift.py listed runs/eval/deepseek_lab/wrecked/shift.py as a graph neighbour and printed its symbols. That file is the DESTROYED artefact kept as evidence: a test module that overwrote the real one. Showing it to a model asked to edit shift.py teaches it precisely the substitution the write gate now refuses -- the brief would have been arguing for the bug. * build/ -- holds 142 stale copies of the package. Every naive sweep double-counts them, and a brief that lists a symbol twice from two versions of one file is worse than one that omits it.
claims.why: The specific historical events and counts (142 stale copies) are not verifiable from this chunk.

claims.text: Characters reserved for the header, which is composed after the layers are budgeted. Generous on purpose: overshooting the reserve wastes a few hundred characters, while under-reserving silently pushes the brief over the budget a caller sized its prompt against.
claims.why: No header composition logic is visible in this chunk.

claims.text: Top-level API of one Python file, as declaration lines. Signatures rather than bare names, because the measured failure was not only 'the module does not exist' but 'the module does not define that': a name without its shape still lets a caller invent the arguments. Methods are included one level down for classes, since Shift.tick() is the kind of thing a caller needs and the class name alone does not give it. Deeper nesting is deliberately not listed -- it is not API.
claims.why: The function returns signatures (via _sig) for top-level functions, classes with their methods one level down, and uppercase assignments. It does not recurse deeper. The docstring accurately describes the implementation visible in this chunk.

claims.text: Dotted module names this file imports ONLY inside a function body. Computed here rather than read from the index because the index publishes a flat edge list with no depth: it correctly INCLUDES function-body edges (12 edges for offload.py against 7 top-level import statements -- verified), it just cannot say which ones they are. One extra AST pass over a handful of neighbour files buys the distinction.
claims.why: The specific numbers (12 edges for offload.py, 7 top-level imports) are not verifiable from this chunk.

claims.text: Does any dotted name in the set plausibly denote rel? Suffix matching on the dotted path, because a function-body import may be written from .kairos import drafts or import daedalus.kairos.drafts and both denote daedalus/kairos/drafts.py. Over-matching here only ever adds a * mark to an edge that is genuinely present, so a wrong guess mislabels a true edge rather than inventing one.
claims.why: The function implements suffix matching on the last one or two components of the dotted path against the relative file path. The docstring's description of behaviour matches the code.

claims.text: Build the brief for targets and their hops-hop neighbourhood. index may be supplied to avoid a rebuild; otherwise the process-wide cached index is used, which is single-flight, so two hundred concurrent lanes warm it once rather than each starting a full scan. That property is the difference between this being free and this being the reason a fan-out melts the box. Never raises for a missing or unreadable index: a lane that cannot get a brief must still be able to run with none. A brief is context, not a gate.
claims.why: The implementation of index caching and error handling is not fully visible in this chunk (the function is truncated). The claim about never raising is not verifiable from this partial code.

observations.what: Module docstring makes specific claims about historical measurements (202 of 526 internal edges, 6,479 characters for symbol layer, etc.) that cannot be verified from the code in this chunk.
The function graph_brief is incomplete in this chunk; the rest of its implementation is in chunk 2.

The function _deep_only_modules uses ast.walk, which visits all descendant nodes. For a large file, this could be computationally expensive, but the docstring says it's used only over 'a handful of neighbour files'.

The function _tail_matches uses suffix matching which may over-match; the docstring acknowledges this and states it only adds a * mark to a genuinely present edge. However, over-matching could still mislabel edges as deep when they are also present at top level.
The GraphBrief dataclass has a 'provenance' field with default_factory=dict, but no usage of it is visible in this chunk.
